notes: TMax is far and away the strongest corpus: it is full of custom-compression / reverse-a-codec / write-the-packer tasks, and task_000185 is a near-perfect analog (given the decompressor binary, write the compressor, meet a size budget). The honest final_top10 is therefore all TMax. The other corpora have no 'write a compressor matching a given decompressor' task, so I judged on the two transferable halves: reverse-engineer-a-format (crackme/binary reversing in RTS and TW, pfp binary-template parsing in SWE-Rebench) and codec/round-trip/bit-packing correctness (cantools bit-packing and chardet detection in SWE-Smith, aiohttp ZLibCompressor and celery serializers in SWE-Rebench). RTS's 7-bit-binary-decoder 'parachute' family and its steganography-decode tasks are the closest implement-a-codec-from-spec analogs there. SWE-Smith is the weakest (all overall 1-3). The lexical shortlist was noisy: most 'gzipped tarball' / 'compress the CSV' hits are standard-tool usage with zero codec-authoring content, and I discounted them hard.
